newsitem.title: INDIA: India oil sector so far unaffected by truck strike.
newsitem.headline: India oil sector so far unaffected by truck strike.

text.p: Indian refineries were largely unaffected by a nationwide truckers strike so far but overfull storage capacity could pose problems if the strike continues for long, refining companies's officials said on Thursday.
More than two million trucks have stopped running since owners began their protest against a service tax and surging insurance premiums at midnight on Monday.
"It has not affected (oil industry) so far," an official of Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd (HPCL) said.
He said diesel demand was sharply down because of the truckers' strike. Company-owned trucks and dealer trucks are still running, he said.
Petroleum products are moved partly through pipelines from where company-owned and contractors's trucks take over.
Some trucks hired by contractors were running with police protection, another official said.
"We knew this was coming," said an official at Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL).
He said petrol stations were filled to the brim on March 31, the day before the strike began. The market was yet to feel any shortage and there were no queues at filling stations.
"We can manage for a few days," the official said.
Most metropolitan cities were well connected by pipelines from refineries and would be the last to be affected, Amitabh Sarma, analyst at securities firm SBI Capital Markets, said.
"But small towns will be affected if the strike continues for a week," he said.
Manager at a refinery, who declined to be identified, said a prolonged strike could even lead to a refinery shut-down.
"We will have a problem of storing (products) if there is no movement (of refined products to the market)," he said.
The transport industry's consumption of diesel and motor spirit accounts for almost half of India's total petroleum products consumption.
In 1995/96 (April-March), diesel sale alone constituted 45 percent of total petroleum product consumption, analysts said.
"HSD (high speed diesel) demand was much higher than motor spirit on account of HSD being a subsidised product and motor spirit overpriced," SBI Capital Markets said in a recent report.
Diesel and kerosene are subsidised under India's government-fixed administered pricing mechanism.
